Loss-of-function mutations in AP4S1 (causing MONDO:0013552) and AP4B1 (causing MONDO:0013551) impair the function of the adaptor protein complex AP-4. This leads to defects in vesicular transport (GO:0006898), specifically disrupting the trafficking of essential proteins and cargo required for autophagosome-lysosome fusion (GO:0000282). The resulting cellular dysfunction contributes to the shared phenotypes of spastic paraplegia (HP:0001256) and intellectual disability (HP:0001249).

**How to falsify it:** The hypothesis would be falsified if mutations in AP4S1 and AP4B1 were found to be completely unlinked to cellular processes involving vesicular transport or autophagosome-lysosome fusion, or if the shared phenotypes could be attributed to entirely separate molecular pathways. _(variant: Common variants in AP4S1 or AP4B1 with a frequency >1% in gnomAD that are shown to cause either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of the AP-4 complex in vesicular trafficking and lysosomal function offers a potential therapeutic target for both MONDO:0013552 and MONDO:0013551, potentially through strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing autophagosome-lysosome fusion or mitigating downstream cellular deficits.
